title: Introduce first-class lease auth profiles, named retry flavors, and pullstream clarifications across SDKs
author: Asha Menon
description:
Context and motivation: We've received recurring feedback that SDK consumers want an explicit, ergonomic concept for short-lived auth leases, and a small set of named retry profiles that can be wire-mapped across Python/TS/Go to avoid subtle divergence. This PR introduces a lightweight 'lease' lifecycle API (acquire/renew/release/annotate) and a compact mapping of retry 'flavors' (optimistic, balanced, aggressive) that the SDKs expose in parity. It also clarifies pullstream semantics: deprecates the older opaque resume-token surface in favor of a checkpoint cursor and documents recommended migration paths.

What this changes (high level):
- Adds a Lease abstraction to SDK core (py/ts/go) + low-overhead heartbeat shim for long-running streams.
- Introduces named retry flavors and a small declarative adapter so platform defaults can be propagated across languages.
- Pullstream: replace ResumeToken v1 surface with CheckpointCursor v2; provide compat shim that translates legacy tokens at runtime to minimize breakage.
- Adds cross-sdk integration tests that exercise lease renewals during streaming disconnects.
- Minor telemetry/metrics labels to differentiate lease renewals vs token refreshes for cost/ops visibility.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests added, [x] cross-sdk integration tests, [x] update changelogs/versions, [x] migration notes for users.

review_threads:
Diego Rivera: This design looks sensible; can we make the Lease.renew() non-blocking by default? Some consumers run renewals on a background timer and expect a soft failure path.
Asha: Good catch — changed renew() to accept {blocking?: boolean} and added a lightweight callback hook for errors.

Lena Hoffmann: Strong +1 on named retry flavors but request: ensure the mapping to underlying backoff multipliers is documented and not changed silently.
Asha: Added explicit constants doc block and an integration test that asserts the mapping is stable.

Marcus Lee: There's a race in the Go shim when legacy ResumeToken joins a stream mid-lease. Requesting an explicit test and a short delay backoff.
Asha: Added test 'TestCompatResumeDuringLease' and a 150ms jittered backoff in the shim to avoid thundering renewals.
requested_changes: Add non-blocking renew API and ensure all SDKs expose an ergonomic default
Document retry flavor mappings and add integration asserts
Add compatibility test for resume-token -> checkpoint conversion under lease churn

Added docs/runtime assertions for retry flavor mapping and a changelog note

merge_details: Merged by Marcus Lee on 2025-11-10 using squash merge. Commit message consolidated core changes, included migration notes. Shortest commit title: 'sdk: lease + retry flavors + pullstream checkpoint (cross-sdk)'.
release_notes:
- Introduce Lease API (acquire/renew/release/annotate) across Python/TypeScript/Go.
- Add named retry flavors (optimistic, balanced, aggressive) and documented mappings.
- Pullstream: CheckpointCursor v2 introduced; compat shim provided for ResumeToken v1.
- Cross-SDK integration tests for lease renewals and resume compatibility.
- SDK version bumps: python 0.22.0, typescript 1.12.0, go v0.9.1.
notes: This PR intentionally provides a compat shim for ResumeToken v1 to avoid an immediate breaking migration. We plan to mark ResumeToken v1 deprecated in the next minor release and remove the shim in one major cycle. Ops: added telemetry labels lease.renew and lease.acquire to help SREs tune defaults.
